articles.headline: Erik ten Hag: Man United being relegated is 'certainly possible'
articles.description: Erik ten Hag has told ESPN that Manchester United being relegated from the Premier League this season is "certainly possible."
articles.headlineJa: エリック・テン・ハフ：マン・Uの降格は「間違いなく起こり得る」
articles.descriptionJa: エリック・テン・ハフはESPNに対し、今シーズンのマンチェスター・ユナイテッドのプレミアリーグ降格は「間違いなく起こり得る」と語った。
articles.body:
Erik ten Hag has told ESPN that Manchester United being relegated from the Premier League this season is "certainly possible" after his former side slipped to 17th in the table on Saturday.

Only United's goal difference has United out of the drop zone after they suffered a 2-0 defeat to Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on Saturday in a result that piled further pressure on head coach Michael Carrick. 

United have not been relegated since 1974 and, despite there being plenty of time left to turn things around this season, are now contemplating the once unthinkable prospect of a relegation battle. They face Aston Villa and Liverpool in their next two league games.

Ten Hag was in charge at Old Trafford from April 2022 to November 2024. After finishing third in his first season in charge, United dropped to eighth in 2023-24 and the Dutch manager only lasted until November the following season as he was sacked with the club in 14th place.

He led United to the Carabao Cup in 2022-23 and the FA Cup a year later.

- Ogden: Man United implode at Chelsea; they are now in Premier League relegation battle

Asked if he sees United being relegated as a possible scenario come May on ESPN NL's Goedemorgen Eredivisie, Ten Hag said: "In the Premier League it's certainly possible, because all the teams are simply strong.

"They're all strong squads, all good managers. And if you end up on the wrong side once and you really get into that vicious circle -- yes, then it can become very, very difficult."

Ten Hag, who is now the technical director of Dutch side FC Twente, also had some choice words for Cristiano Ronaldo's application and fitness during their time together as he reflected on his time at Old Trafford.

"I think we performed pretty well with United," Ten Hag said. "I think we had performed more than pretty well. We couldn't have done it better. 

"Before we arrived, six years without winning a trophy. Look where they are now. We were at Wembley six times, we played two FA Cup finals. We won 2 trophies, we finished third. And yes, we simply performed pretty well. And at times we also played pretty good football.

"We also had a difficult spell... But the Premier League is so strong and when you hit a difficult spell, yes, then you really have a problem."

articles.body:
It's the first day of November, and we've got a massive Premier League showdown on our hands as Liverpool welcome Arsenal to Anfield in a clash between two of England's biggest clubs.

The defending champions have won seven of their opening eight league matches, and Mikel Arteta's side will be looking to maintain their strong start to the season. However, they face a Liverpool side finding its rhythm under Andoni Iraola, with the Reds hoping to close the six-point gap between the teams.

There's also plenty of history at stake, with Arsenal looking to secure their first Premier League win at Anfield since 2012.

Plus, follow along for all the best goals and highlights from elsewhere in Europe, as Real Madrid face Racing Santander.

articles.headline: Erik ten Hag questions Cristiano Ronaldo's fitness, ability at Man United: 'From Juventus onwards it's simply over'
articles.description: Erik ten Hag has told ESPN he does not believe Cristiano Ronaldo was fit or committed enough during their time together at Manchester United.
articles.headlineJa: エリック・テン・ハフ、マンUでのクリスティアーノ・ロナウドのコンディションと能力に疑問：「ユベントス以降、単に終わっていた」
articles.descriptionJa: エリック・テン・ハフはESPNに対し、マンチェスター・ユナイテッドでの共演期間中、クリスティアーノ・ロナウドのフィットネスや献身性は十分ではなかったと考えていると語った。
articles.body:
Erik ten Hag has told ESPN he does not believe Cristiano Ronaldo was fit or committed enough during their time together at Manchester United, adding that he feels the five-time Ballon d'Or winner could "no longer deliver" on the pitch after leaving Juventus in 2021.

Ten Hag also said the notion that one of Ronaldo's defining characteristics is his dedication to pushing his physical limits is "not entirely true, but that is the image."

Ronaldo left Juventus to return to Old Trafford where he scored 27 goals in a 54-game spell under Ole Gunnar Solskjaer and then Ten Hag. 

- Erik ten Hag: Man United being relegated is 'certainly possible'

The former Ajax boss did not see eye to eye with the Portugal star during the latter stages of his time in charge at United as he regularly opted to leave Ronaldo out of the starting XI.

United terminated Ronaldo's contract in November 2022 after he said in an interview with Piers Morgan that he felt "betrayed" by the Dutch manager and criticised the club's hierarchy. 

Ten Hag, who is now the technical director of Dutch side FC Twente, was sacked nine games into the 2023-24 season with United 14th in the Premier League table. 

Reflecting on his time at the club, Ten Had told ESPN NL's Goedemorgen Eredivisie on Sunday: "The challenge is to get the team functioning, really as always. Every player is important in that and you need top players to be able to win. Every top team must embrace the top player, but the top player must work for the team. And that was simply the problem with Ronaldo."

- Why Cristiano Ronaldo's 982nd career goal should be an own goal

He continued: "The players wanted to work for him and they looked up to him because let there be no misunderstanding about that. He is of course a tremendous player, one of the greats of all time. But that is also the reality over the last seven, eight years he simply can no longer deliver. From Juventus onwards it's simply over.

"And that is actually the great gift of Real Madrid -- they always know when to say goodbye to players at the right moment. They recognise when a player's level is declining and they say goodbye at a moment when to the outside world, they still appear to be at their peak. But they can no longer actually deliver."

Ronaldo was 36 by the time he returned to the Premier League and was criticised by commentators and pundits for his perceived inability to press opposition defenders. 

Rather than putting Ronaldo's physical decline down to his advancing years, Ten Hag said the former Real Madrid forward "could no longer bring himself to push through the pain."

"I naturally gave him a special status," Ten Hag said. "I also went to him, I spoke to him prior to that job, I explained to him how we were going to play, what his role in that would be, what I expected of him, and what he could expect from me and from the team. But ultimately you also have to deliver yourself and he was no longer capable of pushing himself to the limit.

articles.body:
Halloween on Saturday could see players around the NFL thinking scary and spooky when it comes to their outfits.

That doesn't mean the cozy looks meant for colder weather aren't an option, though. Hoodies, jackets and long sleeves have been a common choice in the past weeks, and that didn't change this time around. T-shirts aren't out of style either, often complete with an oversized jacket for warmth. 

However one decides to dress for their pregame arrival can make its own headlines. That was the case in Week 8, too.

Here's a look at the top fits across the NFL. 

Sunday's best

Minnesota Vikings' quarterback Kyler Murray and wide receiver Justin Jefferson reported to their duties in similar monochromatic looks, with Murray styling a double-breasted look with a white tank and a beanie to match.

Thursday night fashion

Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young opted for a clean Louis Vuitton shirt with a heavy jacket on top and sleek sunglasses. On the other side, Green Bay Packers safety Javon Bullard went with a denim tie shirt from the clothing brand Jagne.

articles.headline: Jude Bellingham becomes first Englishman to score 50 goals for Real Madrid
articles.description: Jude Bellingham became the first Englishman to score 50 goals for Real Madrid as Jose Mourinho's side raced into a 3-0 first-half lead at Racing Santander.
articles.headlineJa: ジュード・ベリンガム、レアル・マドリードで50ゴールを達成した初のイングランド人選手に
articles.descriptionJa: レーシング・サンタンデルの試合で、ジョゼ・モウリーニョ率いるチームが前半に3点のリードを奪う中、ジュード・ベリンガムはレアル・マドリードで50ゴールを記録した初のイングランド人選手となった。
articles.body:
Jude Bellingham became the first Englishman to score 50 goals for Real Madrid as José Mourinho's side raced into a 3-0 first-half lead at Racing Santander.

Bellingham snapped a seven-match scoring drought with his side's second goal of the afternoon, after Kylian Mbappé had earlier scored a penalty for Real Madrid.

Yan Diomande then added a third goal for Real Madrid after 36 minutes as Los Blancos continued their good form after El Clásico glory last weekend.

Bellingham was already the highest-scoring English player for Real Madrid, with David Beckham and Laurie Cunningham tied on 20 for second place.

articles.headline: Jalen Brunson joins Harry Styles on stage to cap Styles' MSG residency
articles.description: The superstar singer-songwriter was joined on stage by Brunson, who presented Styles with a commemorative banner for his 30-show Madison Square Garden residency.
articles.headlineJa: ジェイレン・ブランソンがハリー・スタイルズのステージに登場、MSGレジデンシーの締めくくりに
articles.descriptionJa: 超人気シンガーソングライターのステージにブランソンが共演。マディソン・スクエア・ガーデンでの30公演にわたるレジデンシーを記念して、スタイルズに記念バナーを贈呈した。
articles.body:
Harry Styles brings plenty of fame to the stage as-is, but the superstar singer-songwriter's Saturday night performance at Madison Square Garden got an extra boost in star power from a guest plenty familiar with the Garden's spotlight.

Star New York Knicks guard Jalen Brunson.

Saturday night marked the 30th show of Styles' Together, Together residency, and he was joined on stage by Brunson, who presented Styles with a commemorative banner for the residency. Brunson, who was received with uproarious "MVP" chants from the home crowd, rocked a hat emblazoned with "TECHNO IS MY BOYFRIEND," which Styles has been known to don himself.

"Can you just make a note, we're almost as tall as each other," Styles joked when the two greeted each other on stage.

"And, yes, I will return your hat," Brunson responded.

It's not the first time during Styles' residency that Brunson has made an appearance. The newly minted NBA champion had already attended two of Styles' previous shows during his stretch of performances at the Garden, getting a shoutout from the singer on Sept. 12.

"We may or may not have the King of New York in the house tonight ... Mr. Jalen Brunson," Styles said during the show. "He's just trying to have a quiet night out -- not a chance. Not in this city. It's like Mickey Mouse going to Disneyland."

Brunson will return to his own Madison Square Garden stage Monday when the Knicks host the Brooklyn Nets.

ESPN's basketball daily cheat sheet is your pregame destination before you lock in daily fantasy and betting decisions for that night's games. Here you'll find our top insights for the slate, including players to target for your daily fantasy rosters, along with game-by-game injury reports.

What you need to know for Sunday

November opens with a quartet of NBA games, each of which could prove to be competitive according to betting metrics, as today's point spreads range from just 2.5-6.5 points.

Tighter lines suggest the potential for close games, a welcome environment for fantasy purposes given the greater predictability of playing time and workloads when games are tight and coaching patterns remain steadier.

The action opens with the Orlando Magic hosting the Boston Celtics in a matinee. We won't see Boston's Mitchell Robinson due to planned rest, while Paolo Banchero and Jalen Suggs are sidelined for the Magic. Learn about a rising two-way Magic guard in the streaming section below.

The Indiana Pacers host the Brooklyn Nets in a contest with a lengthy injury report. The absence of Tyrese Haliburton and Ivica Zubac for the Pacers spells another big role for combo guard Andrew Nembhard. Third-year forward Jarace Walker could help in deeper leagues thanks to his ability to do a little bit of everything.

The LA Clippers' decline includes being underdogs to a Golden State Warriors team that won't have Stephen Curry or Draymond Green due to respective injury-management plans. This all points to a big role for Yaxel Lendeborg, who has proven to be one of the most productive rookies in an already impressive class.

The slate concludes with the Los Angeles Lakers hosting the Toronto Raptors. Kawhi Leonard's knee issues resurfaced recently, putting the offense back in the hands of Scottie Barnes. The Lakers are looking to make up for Friday's embarrassing loss to the Warriors and should field a full roster.

With an eye toward uncovering compelling betting angles and fantasy decisions, let's take a look at the day ahead in the NBA.

Fantasy stream team -- widely available players worth adding

Anthony Black, PG/SG, Magic (rostered in 43.3% of ESPN leagues)

Last season, it took a series of injuries to high-usage teammates for Black to emerge as a difference-making statistical force. With Banchero and Suggs both sitting, Black is back in pole position to produce. Among the league leaders in drives when he was initiating offense for Orlando last spring, there are several paths to impressive numbers for Black this afternoon.

The Clippers are using a committee of forwards to handle frontcourt duties this season. Jackson is emerging from the crowd with active defensive play and helpful, connective passing from the high post. articles.headline: Fantasy football flex and superflex rankings for Week 8
articles.description: Trying to decide between a couple of closely ranked players this week? Eric Karabell's rankings are here to help.
articles.body:
Welcome to Week 8 of the 2026 NFL season and our weekly PPR fantasy football superflex rankings. We know many of you compete in superflex formats that invite/covet second quarterbacks in starting lineups, and these rankings account for that. It might look odd to see the lowest-ranked fantasy passers ahead of typical RB2 and WR2 options, but the potential scoring impact demands it.

If your league is a standard flex, note that rankings without QBs appear below the superflex rankings. However you prefer to play, good luck this week!

These ranks have been refreshed to take out players from Thursday's Panthers-Packers game.

Teams on bye in Week 8: 49ers, Giants, Saints, Texans

Week 8 superflex rankings (includes quarterbacks)

 1. Jahmyr Gibbs, RB1 vs MIN

The Vikings are the best defensive team, but Gibbs is the best player in fantasy. Try not to think about it.
 2. Josh Allen, QB1 vs BAL

Again, matchups may not matter to him, but he should be able to shred the Ravens defense.
 3. Jaxon Smith-Njigba, WR1 vs CHI

The schedule isn't an issue here. He plays Monday against the Bears.
 4. Drake Maye, QB2 @ MIA

Worry about his schedule in a month. For this week, enjoy the numbers against the Dolphins.
 5. Joe Burrow, QB3 vs TEN

He has increased his fantasy point total in each game this season. Can the Titans end the streak?
 6. Lamar Jackson, QB4 @ BUF

Expect he (finally) returns from a sprained ankle, but do not presume he runs. 
 7. Jayden Daniels, QB5 vs PHI

 8. Puka Nacua, WR2 vs LAC

 9. Ja'Marr Chase, WR3 vs TEN

 10. Trevor Lawrence, QB6 vs IND

 11. Dak Prescott, QB7 vs ARI

He looked great against the Eagles, and he should look great against the Cardinals this week.
 12. Kenneth Walker III, RB2 @ DEN

The Seahawks stymied him, now come the Broncos. Walker ran for 173 yards against Denver in Week 1.
 13. Bijan Robinson, RB3 @ TB

The Buccaneers are stout versus the run, but this isn't a typical running back. Don't worry.
 14. Javonte Williams, RB4 vs ARI

The Cowboys showed Monday that they can run the football. They just have to stick with this plan.
 15. James Cook III, RB5 vs BAL

 16. CeeDee Lamb, WR4 vs ARI

 17. Zay Flowers, WR5 @ BUF

 18. Amon-Ra St. Brown, WR6 vs MIN

 19. Drake London, WR7 @ TB

He has double-digit targets in four of five games. Let's assume the Falcons keep that going. 
 20. Justin Jefferson, WR8 @ DET

Two good games, three bad ones this season. One would think facing the Lions will be a good game.
 21. Trey McBride, TE1 @ DAL

Only two wide receivers have more fantasy points this season. This is an historic player.
 22. Matthew Stafford, QB8 vs LAC

He faces the Chargers. They're bad, but they do play decent defense. Don't assume Stafford has a monster game.
 23. Derrick Henry, RB6 @ BUF

The Bills permit ample fantasy points to running backs. If Henry struggles, it is time for concern.

articles.headline: Robert De Zerbi on Tottenham revival: 'Now we are playing as a team'
articles.description: Roberto De Zerbi believes Tottenham's turnaround in the Premier League is down to his new-look squad now being a team.
articles.headlineJa: ロベルト・デ・ゼルビが語るトッテナム復活：「今、私たちはチームとしてプレーできている」
articles.descriptionJa: ロベルト・デ・ゼルビは、プレミアリーグにおけるトッテナムの好転は、刷新されたスカッドが真の「チーム」になったことによるものだと考えている。
articles.body:
Roberto De Zerbi believes Tottenham's turnaround in the Premier League is down to his new-look squad now being a team.

Spurs produced a professional display to beat 10-man Crystal Palace by a 2-0 score on Saturday to win three consecutive league games for the first time in 616 days.

A trip to Marbella last month has been the catalyst for this form and after £380 million ($509m) was committed on 10 new signings this summer by majority owners the Lewis family, De Zerbi believes Tottenham are finally a team again.

"I think even before the national break we were playing well," De Zerbi said.

"We were playing maybe not 90 minutes, but many parts of the game we played very well. We didn't score. We conceded a stupid goal and then we lost energy. We lost spirit. We lost the right union between the players.

"If we compare Tottenham before the national break and Tottenham after the national break, now we are playing as a team.

"Before the national break we were playing as many very good players, but not as a team."

The growing camaraderie in this Spurs side has been evident and was again on Saturday with opening scorer Archie Gray mobbed by the home substitutes on the sideline after his 25th-minute headed goal.

Gray produced another accomplished display at right-back on the ninth occasion the 20-year-old has started out of position this season.

De Zerbi took off Gray at half-time, but it was down to a yellow card in the 15th minute.

"He's improving a lot. After Manchester United, he's playing very, very well and as a mature player," De Zerbi said.

"I didn't want to take a risk for another yellow card. I'm sorry because he was playing very well.

"I explained why I took the decision, but I think it was the right decision in that moment."

Gray's growing comfort at right-back has allowed De Zerbi and Tottenham to be patient with World Cup winner Pedro Porro, who missed the start of the campaign with a hamstring issue.

The same injury was aggravated in a September defeat to Aston Villa, but Porro is fit again and will be ready to start next week's trip to Leeds if required.

De Zerbi explained: "Pedro is ready. We didn't take risks. Speaking with him, he decided before the game [to not start] and he was very honest with me.

"And I appreciate a lot because the Premier League is 38 games, not one game."

- Tottenham's resurgence continues with win over 10-man Palace 

- Under-fire Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage: 'I will never give up'

Porro and Destiny Udogie featured in tandem on opposite flanks during the second half in another sign of Spurs' improved squad depth.

Both have been crucial to De Zerbi's predecessors, but given Udogie has struggled with multiple fitness problems, the free signing of Andy Robertson in June has alleviated Spurs' reliance on the Italian.

Robertson has produced a string of consistent performances and De Zerbi has challenged Udogie to stay fit for a sustained period.

articles.headline: Mavericks face the Kings on 3-game win streak
articles.description: Sacramento Kings (0-6, 15th in the Western Conference) vs. Dallas Mavericks (4-2, seventh in the Western Conference)
articles.headlineJa: 3連勝中のマーベリックス、キングスと対戦
articles.descriptionJa: サクラメント・キングス（0勝6敗、ウェスタン・カンファレンス15位）対 ダラス・マーベリックス（4勝2敗、ウェスタン・カンファレンス7位）
articles.body:
Sacramento Kings (0-6, 15th in the Western Conference) vs. Dallas Mavericks (4-2, seventh in the Western Conference)


              Dallas; Monday, 8 p.m. EST


              BOTTOM LINE: Dallas will look to keep its three-game win streak intact when the Mavericks take on Sacramento.


              Dallas went 26-56 overall and 14-37 in Western Conference play a season ago. The Mavericks averaged 114.1 points per game while shooting 46.6% from the field and 34.4% from 3-point distance last season.


              Sacramento went 22-60 overall and 14-38 in Western Conference games during the 2025-26 season. The Kings shot 46.7% from the field and 34.0% from 3-point range last season.


              INJURIES: Mavericks: Santi Aldama: day to day (knee), Tarik Biberovic: day to day (heel), Sergio De Larrea: out (knee), Dereck Lively II: day to day (foot).


              Kings: Ben Simmons: out for season (achilles), Keegan Murray: out (ankle), Dylan Cardwell: out (calf), Maxime Raynaud: out (knee).


              ------

articles.headline: Chicago faces Philadelphia, looks to stop 4-game skid
articles.description: Chicago Bulls (1-5, 13th in the Eastern Conference) vs. Philadelphia 76ers (6-1, first in the Eastern Conference)
articles.body:
Chicago Bulls (1-5, 13th in the Eastern Conference) vs. Philadelphia 76ers (6-1, first in the Eastern Conference)


              Philadelphia; Monday, 7:30 p.m. EST


              BOTTOM LINE: Chicago aims to break its four-game skid with a victory against Philadelphia.


              Philadelphia finished 45-37 overall, 27-25 in Eastern Conference play and 23-18 at home during the 2025-26 season. The 76ers averaged 18.9 points off of turnovers, 15.4 second-chance points and 32.4 bench points last season.


              Chicago finished 31-51 overall and 19-32 in Eastern Conference games during the 2025-26 season. The Bulls shot 46.9% from the field and 35.6% from 3-point range last season.


              INJURIES: 76ers: Ariel Hukporti: out for season (achilles), LeBron James: out (back), Joel Embiid: out (foot), Dominick Barlow: out (back).


              Bulls: Dailyn Swain: day to day (back), Nic Claxton: out (hamstring).


              ------
